decisions.rationale: Owner chose it after measurement resolved a direct contradiction between two consultants. context_notes: TWO PRIOR-HANDOFF UNVERIFIED CLAIMS WERE MEASURED THIS SESSION AND BOTH CAME OUT AGAINST THE EARLIER INFERENCE. First, 'the important-tier findings would largely dissolve under option 1' -- measured, only 1 of the 9 named findings sits in the cut region; 8 survive. Second, 'ship the milestone without the taxonomy' -- not available, but for an unrelated reason: EVL-03 is pending on a metered run and 21-SECURITY.md and 21-LEARNINGS.md do not exist. WHAT WENT RIGHT, worth repeating. The brief-versus-authority diff caught a real omission before dispatch, which is exactly the failure that cost the prior round. The unprimed critic, given only the owner's verbatim words and no proposal, independently produced a plan close to the primed advisor's and separately flagged the two clauses most likely to be misread -- both flags held, and it also detected a gap in its own brief unprompted. The plan-checker reported OBSERVED EXIT CODES rather than readings of commands, and that is how BLOCKER-1 surfaced. MY OWN ERRORS THIS SESSION, all caught: I asserted the taxonomy prose 'loads in every real coaching turn' from the link alone, and measurement showed the coach decision procedure never routes to it; I relayed a consultant's mockist mis-citation claim at full strength when the evidence supported only PLAUSIBLE; and my escaped-pipe check used shell escaping that degenerated and matched all 141 lines of a file, which I caught only because the sample rows made no sense. The pattern in all three is the one this whole task is about -- a check that reports a result without verifying the thing it names.
